raw_text:
Plan intended to elaborate on an example of a 'repeated responses to the same question' research objective hypothesis that you stated in the discussion.


Identify what needs to hold constant and/or what needs to be changed to observe corresponding effects and to test linked explanations. Spell out the null hypothesis you decided is most appropriate for your objective. State alternative hypotheses for rejection and failure to reject the null, as appropriate for the research purpose.

Where possible, review at least 2 suites of parameters. Additional parameters – other parameters on which explanations are readily linked – should be listed.

Research Plan

Plan - what research you will need to do. This is a list of things you will try and then assess what you conclude from it. You can have multiple plans.


Research Plan


The most precise definitions of D/P/B you can think of for your hypotheses. Any other variables that behave differently for the 3 hypotheses? If the definition is a numeric one, make sure you can unambiguously calculate intermediate values such that their differences are very small for the hypothesis situations. Observations/drawings/figures etc might help here. The analysis requires that the measurement precision is well specified, at the least in terms of inflection points before and after small differences.

- If the definition is a description, specify/indicate features that aid observations, existence checks, and maybe explanatory controls; and just note quality.

First, define or sketch all variables needed to instantiate the null hypothesis and discern the differences between it and the other alternatives. For example: Include features being observed, measured, likely durations for which the experiments will run, and their primary and secondary performance correlates.

Second, note whether any of the contextual differences among alternatives need different parameter values, reference classes, or selective inducers for the D/P/B/Porenthods respectively to avoid confound variables.

Third, note whether the alternatives may generate confound or biased observables, and how those would be removed - especially for selectivities.

Fourth, note whether control information will be in and/or out of scope for any selection effects or selective inducer effects.


Generally, any differences among the alternatives' D/P/B parameters?

If yes, what features might distinguish the changes and/or explain them.

How results will be quantified – i.e. analyzing the effects of changing something.

How will the results be determined evident? Are you comparing just one difference set or will it be considered with/against other difference sets?

What is the forcing function or objective of the analysis?
